passages.note: Bill overview shows SCR1040's instrument and chamber vote tallies; it names no individual actor on this page.
House Third Reading vote list shows Livingston voted Y on the amended SCR1040.

passages.provision_quote: For any employee who customarily and regularly receives tips or gratuities from patrons or others, the employer may pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute if the employer can establish by the employer's records of charged tips or gratuities or by the employee’s declaration for federal insurance contributions act purposes that for each week, when adding tips or gratuities received to wages paid, the employee received not less than the minimum wage plus $2 for all hours worked.
passages.note: The engrossed bill's operative section creates a tip credit for tipped workers, not a general wage-floor change.

rows.reasoning: SCR1040's operative section lets an employer pay a tipped employee up to 25% per hour less than the statutory minimum wage, offset by tips so the employee nets at least "the minimum wage plus $2"; this is a tip-credit carve-out, not the ladder's question of whether to index, raise, localize, hold, or remove the general wage floor, so every passage is adjacent under V2. Livingston voted Y on the House Third Reading ("Passed 35-24-0-0-1 Amended"), but no rung's text matches the tip-credit clause, so the row is BLANK no-evidence.
